promotion_note: PROMOTED 2026-07-31 (nyiso-105). NYISO keeper -> 2026-07-31-nyiso105-chp-heat-rates (bundle results/calibration/nyiso105_chpheatrate_B, DETERMINATION CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS, 0 FAILs, 1 ledgered caveat: C3c price tail — the SAME determination and the SAME single caveat the nyiso-100 keeper carried, and NO new caveat slot is spent). ONE delta vs the nyiso-100 keeper: measured_chp_heat_rates. It adds ZERO free parameters — it replaces one measured input with a strictly more accurate measured input on the SAME source, vintage and net denominator: eGRID's own published CHP heat-input allocation, undone (heat_rate = (PLHTIAN + CHPCHTI) / PLNGENAN). For a cogeneration plant eGRID does not publish PLHTRT as total fuel per net MWh — it first removes the fuel it attributes to useful thermal output — so the incumbent rate made CHP the cheapest thermal on the system. NO gross-to-net factor is involved, which is exactly what blocked the CEMS route (FINDING-miso98 §6.1). ARTIFACT: 31 (plant, class) rows derived, 18 applied on flag=='ok' — CC_CHP 11/17 plants (2,984 of 4,309 MW = 69.3 %) 6.82 -> 8.50 MMBtu/MWh (incumbent understated 19.8 %), CT_CHP 7/14 plants (384 of 446 MW = 86.2 %) 7.46 -> 11.68 (understated 36.2 %); largest repricings are in-city (Linden 915 MW 5.74 -> 9.23, East River 306 MW 7.42 -> 11.80, Brooklyn Navy Yard 260 MW 5.38 -> 8.75). Independently validated: (PLHTIAN + CHPCHTI) reproduces metered CAMPD heat input within 1 % on 16 of 18 covered plants, median ratio 1.00000. Rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: derived from NYISO's own plants; no MISO/CAISO value crossed the boundary, and NYISO is NOT in CHP_STEAM_CREDIT_HR_CORRECTION_ISOS ({CAISO, PJM}) so no hand factor is involved — unlike caiso-147 this is a pure rule-14 [R-ACCURATE] accuracy swap, not a hand-number retirement. EVERY PRE-REGISTERED GATE PASSES (results/calibration/PREREG-nyiso105-chp-heat-rates-2026-07-31.md, committed AND PUSHED before either arm solved). Scored against a same-HEAD zero-delta CONTROL (2026-07-31-nyiso105-control), never the committed keeper — and K2 passes on the STRICT BYTE basis, not merely the scorecard one: control minus committed keeper is EXACTLY 0.0 on every class in all three years, so unlike caiso-146/neiso-69 there is NO same-HEAD drift for NYISO and the A/B is unconfounded. K3 liveness: class-hour |delta| peaks at CC_CHP 727.0/578.9/660.4 MW, CT_CHP 160.7/157.3/160.7 MW. K4: the run_config scenario blocks differ in exactly the one boolean. K5: both bundles [2023, 2024, 2025] and nothing else — the holdout spend freeze is ACTIVE and untouched. K6: the movement is NOT confined to D-10 pinned classes (CC_REGULAR, ST_GAS and CT_PEAKER all move), so the verdict does not rest on classes D-10 discounts. NO CRITERION REGRESSES, AND TWO THINGS IMPROVE. Every criterion status is identical to the control (fuelmix/sysvol/price_mean/price_shape/dispatch_corr/governance/shape/forced_share PASS, price_tail CAVEAT; C1 all 14/14 / free 10/10). (1) The energy-weighted C1 residual FALLS: 3-year mean |error| 9.458 % -> 9.224 %, per year 7.66 -> 7.60, 5.66 -> 4.76, 15.06 -> 15.31, with more classes better than worse every year (4/3, 5/2, 4/3). CC_CHP +13.61 -> +10.75, +7.95 -> +2.74, +31.41 -> +28.21 %; CC_REGULAR -7.93 -> -6.61 and -1.87 -> +0.23 %; ST_GAS better in 2024 and 2025; CT_PEAKER better in all three. (2) The keeper's OWN D-2 failure CLEARS: nyiso-100 carried '2024 ST_GAS: forced share 30.6 % > 30 %'; this arm has NO D-2 failures, because ST_GAS dispatches more once CHP is priced honestly, so the same forced TWh is a smaller share of a larger class. REPORTED AND NOT PATCHED (rules 1 [R-STRUCT] / 14 [R-ACCURATE]): CT_CHP deepens from -49.3/-52.4/-38.6 % to -67.9/-67.6/-62.0 %. It is an OPEN ROOT-CAUSE ITEM, not a defect of this mechanism — CT_CHP was ALREADY 39-52 % under-dispatched BEFORE the arm, so a strictly more accurate offer EXPOSES a pre-existing miss rather than creating one, and reverting an accurate measured input to hide it is exactly what rule 14 forbids. Named successor lane: the BTM host-steam holdout (chp_btm_pct / chp_grid_pmin_mw) and the CT_CHP must-run treatment, NOT the heat rate. Mean lambda rises 34.660 -> 35.078, 37.667 -> 38.227, 61.974 -> 62.837 $/MWh as expected when in-city CHP is repriced up; C3a stays PASS. C3c IS NOT TARGETED, NOT CLAIMED AND NOT MOVED by this arm — the C3c queue stays closed and the frontier declaration below stands unchanged.

frontier.note: FRONTIER DECLARED + DETERMINATION MOVED NOT-YET -> CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS (owner decision, session nyiso-104: 'I am comfortable with taking c3c as a caveat and calling NYISO calibrated with caveats if we've exhausted options to address scarcity tail'). C3c was the SOLE blocker and every other criterion already PASSED; it is now carried as ONE ledgered caveat (budget 3) via the exceptions block of the keeper's calibration_attestation.json, generated by scripts/gen_nyiso100_attestation.py (the GENERATOR is the source of truth — editing only the emitted JSON is reverted by the next run). THE CAVEAT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE BENCHMARK IS WRONG: the measured RT tail is real (model 3/0/7 h vs actual 10/12/42 h >$300) and the model under-produces it. It records an EXHAUSTED lever queue on a diagnosed structural limitation of the five-zone representation — items 1/1b refused ex-ante on identification (nyiso-94/95), item 5 inert ex-ante (nyiso-93), items 2/3 closed and tested (nyiso-96), the last surviving candidate SCUC load-pocket security commitment + BPCG closed ex-ante on CONTENT not merely access (nyiso-97), import shape refused as an attributed C3c symptom with the seam exonerated (nyiso-99), G-J locality refused ex-ante for want of a representable boundary (nyiso-101). The one nominally-open item (nyiso_iroquois_winter_spread) is blocked on a joint SUMMER scarcity lever, and summer is exactly what is exhausted — nyiso-92 dated the actual RT tail as summer (2025 Jun 23-25 alone = 18 of 42 h; the Jan-2024 storm produced ZERO >$300 hours), capping the winter-fuel lane at ~4-5 h/yr. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT] is why this is a ledger entry and not a mechanism: every remaining way to lift the tail is fitted to the tail residual. RE-OPEN CONDITION, satisfiable: a Capital_Hudson -> Zone-F/Zone-G TOPOLOGY SPLIT makes the sub-zonal load pocket representable — its own owner charter (the ERCOT West/Panhandle class, CLOSED), never a mechanism-flag lever. KEEPER UNCHANGED (2026-07-30-nyiso-100-silretire) and NO SOLVE RAN — this is a scorer-side reclassification on the committed bundle. Holdout: NYISO re-declared in the `complete` (VALIDATION-tier) block of calibration-complete.json — 2022 + the 2018/2020/2021 ladder, NOT training; it is deliberately ABSENT from the new `final` (locked-test) block, so 2019 / H1-2026 stay blocked. The ACTIVE holdout spend freeze independently blocks every out-of-training solve regardless, so nothing is spendable until the owner lifts it.
